title: Antiqua Monumenta Quae Gregorii Turonensis Opera Illustrant
author: Gregory of Tours
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1208.tmp1208.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Nam deauratam aliam, quæ in capsario meo cum duobus calicibus aureis, et cruce similiter anrea , quam Mabuinus fecit, Ecclesiæ meæ do, lego. Simul et omnes lihros meos, præter Evangeliorum lihrum, quem scripsit Hilarius quondam Pictaviensis sacerdos a quem tibi Eufronio fratri et consacerdoti dilectissimo cum praefata theca do, lego, volo, statuo. Memor esto mei, amen.
passages.english: For the other, gilded one, which is in my reliquary-chest together with two golden chalices and a cross likewise of gold, which Mabuinus made, I give and bequeath to my church. Likewise also all my books, except the book of the Gospels which Hilary, formerly priest of Poitiers, wrote, which I give, bequeath, will and appoint to you, Eufronius, my most beloved brother and fellow priest, together with the aforesaid case. Remember me. Amen.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'anrea' read as 'aurea', 'lihros/lihrum' as 'libros/librum'; the stray 'a' after 'sacerdos' is taken as a footnote mark. The first sentence is syntactically incomplete: 'deauratam aliam' (the other gilded [case, theca]) has no verb in its relative clause (probably 'est' is to be understood), and 'Nam' ('for') connects awkwardly. 'Capsario' is taken as a chest or reliquary-store. 'Sacerdos' here likely means bishop, as Hilary was bishop of Poitiers.
